nodes.label: Spec 0003. Control and session data model (Status: Proposed, 2026-11-15)

Spec 0003 core rule: durable authority (which node may take writes) and observed database state (what a probe just saw) are separate; writes are admitted only when configuration, journal and a fresh observation all agree

0003 AC-1 new keys are accepted: each valid-topology* fixture exits 0 in both formats with exactly the valid report of spec 0001; every spec 0001 fixture keeps its result; config_version = 1 alone stays valid
0003 AC-2 one mistake, one finding: each invalid-topology-* fixture except invalid-topology-multiple.toml exits 1 with exactly one finding with the listed code, key, line and column
0003 AC-3 whole configuration (SEC-12): invalid-topology-multiple.toml reports its five findings in one run in the listed order; pool_config::validate stays the only way to a ValidatedConfig
0003 AC-4 no file content in output (SEC-4, SEC-11): CANARY-9f2c7b1e appears in neither stdout, stderr, Debug nor Display for the two canary fixtures; validate opens no file

0003 AC-5 identity map (0001 SC-3, SEC-2): ValidatedConfig::resolve_identity returns the route for an exact principal and database pair and None otherwise; no wildcard, no default; the library half of PRD-001 AC-1

0003 AC-6 identifier and generation types: identifiers refuse text outside their syntax and compare exactly; TopologyEpoch, AuthorityRevision and StartSequence only read, compare and advance by one, never past 9223372036854775807; comparing two kinds does not compile

0003 AC-7 clean startup: no journal and no control.authority_id gives Uninitialized and Closed with authority.uninitialized; plan_bootstrap plans only with fresh fitting observations of every node; a journal the configuration does not name is Unconfirmed

0003 AC-8 missing journal: a witness without a journal is Missing, an unreadable journal is Unreadable, another identity is Mismatch; all closed, and plan_bootstrap refuses with bootstrap.witness_present or bootstrap.store_present

0003 AC-9 conflicting role evidence (0001 SC-8, PRD-006 AC-2, PRD-005 AC-1): every row of walk 3 gives the listed result; only full agreement opens; a second primary or a later timeline asks for the conflict latch
0003 AC-10 restore (PRD-006 AC-3): a journal whose hold is restore_pending is Held and closed with authority.restore_pending whatever the observations say; every row of walk 4 gives the listed result

0003 AC-11 freshness (PRD-005 AC-3): an observation as old as the expiry or sampled later than now is no evidence; pool-control never reads a clock (the grep for Instant::now, SystemTime, std::fs, std::env prints nothing)

0003 AC-12 authority is never derived from observation: over the small domain writer_admission is Open only for the node that is both the approved writer in the journal and the expected_writer in the configuration; Authority, EligiblePrimary, Closed and BootstrapPlan cannot be built outside pool-control

0003 AC-13 workspace and guards (0002 AC-6): exactly three workspace members pool, pool-config and pool-control; pool-control depends only on pool-config; the same sixteen third party packages; check.sh all and prove-checks.sh pass with changed baselines; the W4 addition has two tests

0003 AC-14 records and conventions: every record marked built in this slice exists as a public type whose documentation comment states its restart rule; the shared conventions row 'Identifier and generation types' names the rule
Spec 0003: SEC-14 independent review is met by the scope box Review it (fresh model); the review needs the Control engineer role of the reviewer roster, which a fresh model may hold for code
Spec 0003 Decision: build the decisions as plain, tested code now and leave everything that touches a disk, a socket or a database to the slice that first needs it
nodes.rationale: Decisions marked heavy in the rationale are public contracts or formats on disk; changing one later means a new decision in this spec.

nodes.label: Spec 0003 decision point 1: pool-config gains the keys for [control], [[cluster]], [[node]] and [[identity]], their validation, the identifier and generation types and the identity map lookup

Spec 0003 decision point 2: a third workspace crate crates/pool-control holds the authority model (start classification, bootstrap, writer admission); it reads no file, clock or socket; its tests are the four walks

Spec 0003 decision point 3: the journal (one SQLite file), the bootstrap command, the probe and the admission wiring are specified here and built in scope 004; operation records, backup, reconcile and API in scope 009; fence receipts in scope 010
Spec 0003 decision point 4: no third party dependency is added; SQLite is adopted in scope 004 with its own review of native code and licenses
What this slice builds and where it stops (spec 0003 table: built in scope 003 versus later scopes 004 to 010)

Not in the scope 003 build: any listener, PostgreSQL connection, SQLite, thread, async runtime, new command, change to the valid check-config report, or log event; the forbidden source patterns of rule W3 stay
Records table of spec 0003 (one row per record: owner and plane, lifecycle, source, storage, restart rule, built in; a record never has two sources)
Record Cluster: pool-config ClusterConfig, read by both planes; from the configuration file; read and validated again at restart, nothing remembered; built in 003
Record Node: pool-config NodeConfig, read by both planes; from the configuration file; same restart rule as the cluster record; built in 003
Record Identity route: pool-config IdentityRoute, one entry of the identity map read by the data plane at login; from the configuration file, never a startup parameter (0001 SC-3); built in 003
Record Secret reference: pool-config SecretReference, the key credential_file; built in 003
Record Credential (the secret itself): pool-core wrapper that prints [REDACTED] and cannot be serialized; memory only; read again at restart and its credential generation starts over; built in 004

Record Validated configuration: pool-config ValidatedConfig, made by validate and published whole or not at all (SEC-12); the configuration generation starts at 1 at each start; type in 003, number in 004
Record Verified principal: pool-core, made when frontend authentication succeeds and ended with the session; memory; gone at restart; built in 004
Record Session: pool-core data plane, fields as in the data structures of PRD-001; made at accept, ends at disconnect or error; gone at restart, clients reconnect (0001 SC-5); built in 004
Record Lease: pool-core, made at initial admission, pinned to one frontend until the session ends (0001 SC-1) and never moved; no lease, backend or lease generation survives a restart; built in 004
Record Pool key (backend identity, 0001 SC-2): pool-core, computed at initial admission and compared again at handoff; memory; 004 computes it and 005 partitions reuse by it

Record Virtual cancellation credential: pool-core (0001 SC-9), made per lease from random bytes and revoked before release; never on disk or in telemetry; a cancel request after a restart matches nothing; built in 006

Record Observation: pool-control Observation, one probe sample of one node (role is pg_is_in_recovery(), age from the local monotonic clock); memory; none survives a restart, so admission stays closed until fresh ones exist; type in 003, probe in 004
Record Topology snapshot: built by pool-control and mapped by the daemon into the route view of pool-core; immutable; rebuilt at restart with snapshot generation 1; built in 004

Record Journal identity (the store row): pool-control, one writer; made once by bootstrap with random bytes for the authority ID; SQLite; read first at every start without writing and classified; model in 003, file in 004

Record Approved topology (approved writer, members, conflict latch): pool-control, one row per cluster made by bootstrap; writer and members change only by a reviewed operation; an observation can only add the latch; SQLite; compared with configuration and fresh observations before any write (0001 SC-8)

Record Quarantine: pool-control, set by a promotion or an operator and cleared only by an operation with rejoin evidence; a healthy probe cannot clear it (PRD-006 AC-3); SQLite; model in 003, first writer in 010
Record Membership decision (maintenance, drain, detach): pool-control, set and cleared by operations; SQLite; loaded before any lease is admitted; built in 008 and 009

Record Operation: pool-control; from the authenticated caller and the operation plan; SQLite; a row in a phase that is not final is reconciled before the clusters it names admit anything (SEC-7); built in 009, promotion phases in 010
Record Fence receipt: pool-control, belongs to one operation; from the fencing adapter and its independent check; SQLite; built in 010
Record Audit event: pool-control, appended and never changed, no SQL and no secret; SQLite plus export; kept at restart; built in 009
Spec 0003 naming: a configured PostgreSQL server is a node; a backend is one connection to a node; the Backend record of the control plane page is the Node of the records table

What goes into a backend identity (the 0001 SC-2 pool key parts and their sources: cluster, endpoint node ID, database, actual login role, credential generation, topology epoch, TLS policy, startup profile); the configuration generation is checked at handoff and is not part of the key (PRD-002 AC-4)

What may appear in default telemetry (spec 0003): cluster ID, node ID, identity ID, routing profile, every generation, authority state and admission reason names; never principal, database names, backend login, the credential_file path, host, port, secrets, cancellation credentials or SQL
nodes.rationale: The identity ID exists so a log line can say which mapping was used without naming a login; this table is the permission the log rules of spec 0001 ask for.

nodes.label: Identifier and generation types (shared convention of spec 0003: one type per identifier and generation, built only by a checking function, a generation only reads, compares and advances by one and fails closed at the top, shared types live in pool-config, memory generations are scoped by the start sequence)
ClusterId type (pool-config identifier: 1 to 63 bytes, the first a to z, the rest a to z, 0 to 9, _ or -; built by parse)
NodeId type (pool-config identifier with the ClusterId syntax; never compares with a ClusterId)
IdentityId type (pool-config identifier with the ClusterId syntax; the name an operator gives one identity map entry)
SystemIdentifier type (pool-config: the PostgreSQL system identifier, a whole number from 1 to 18446744073709551615, decimal text with no leading zero)
AuthorityId type (pool-config: 16 bytes, in text exactly 32 characters from 0 to 9 and a to f; names one journal and is not a secret)
TimelineId type (pool-control: the PostgreSQL timeline, a whole number from 1 to 4294967295)

TopologyEpoch type: the topology epoch, one per cluster, starts at 1 at bootstrap, advanced by a change of the approved writer (010) or a reconcile naming another writer (009); survives restart in the journal; compared by the pool key

AuthorityRevision type: the authority revision, one per journal, starts at 1 at bootstrap, advanced by every transaction that changes the approved topology, members, conflict latch, quarantine, a membership decision or the hold; survives restart; every durable mutation names the revision it expects

StartSequence type: the start sequence, one per journal, starts at 0 at bootstrap, advanced by each daemon start that finds its journal Ready before anything is admitted; survives restart; scopes every memory generation
Generations table of spec 0003 (where each generation starts, what advances it, whether it survives a restart, who compares it)

Configuration generation in spec 0003: a type created in 004 in pool-config, starts at 1 at each start, advanced by each validated configuration the daemon publishes (a rejected reload does not advance it, PRD-010 AC-2); does not survive a restart

Credential generation in spec 0003: a type created in 004, one per distinct credential_file path, starts at 1 when the file is first read, advanced by a load that reads different bytes or by an explicit revocation; does not survive a restart; compared by the pool key
Snapshot generation in spec 0003: a type created in 004 in pool-control, starts at 1 at each start, advanced by each published topology snapshot; does not survive a restart

Lease generation in spec 0003: a type created in 004 in pool-core, starts at 1 at each start, advanced by each new lease; compared by cancellation and late completions (0001 SC-9); does not survive a restart
Observation has no generation number in spec 0003: it carries its sample time, each probe sample replaces the last one of that node, and evidence is read again fresh when it is needed

What a mutation compares (spec 0003): every durable mutation is one SQLite transaction that starts with BEGIN IMMEDIATE, reads the compared value again and writes nothing when it differs (PRD-006 AC-1); the table lists bootstrap, daemon start, conflict latch, reload, membership changes, reconcile and change of approved writer with the precondition each names
Configuration section of spec 0003 (every new key is optional at the top level, so config_version stays 1 and every file that was valid before is still valid)
[control] table keys: control.state_directory (required when the file has a [[cluster]] entry, path syntax, restart only) and control.authority_id (optional, AuthorityId syntax)
[[cluster]] table keys: cluster[].id (ClusterId, unique), cluster[].system_identifier (a string in SystemIdentifier syntax), cluster[].expected_writer (a NodeId naming a node of this cluster)
[[node]] table keys: node[].id (NodeId, unique in the file), node[].cluster, node[].host (1 to 253 bytes of ASCII letters, digits, '.', '-' or ':') and node[].port (1 to 65535)

[[identity]] table keys: identity[].id, principal, database (the pair is unique), cluster, backend_database (default: the value of database), backend_login, credential_file and routing_profile (default primary)
Key control.state_directory: the directory of the journal (path syntax, restart only); required when the file has at least one cluster

Key control.authority_id: the authority witness, the identity of the journal this configuration belongs to, copied from the output of the bootstrap command; its presence says that a journal was created once
Key cluster[].expected_writer: the operator's statement of which node is the writer; it seeds the approved writer at bootstrap and must keep agreeing with the journal, or writes stay closed

Key identity[].credential_file: the first secret reference in the schema (path syntax); the file is not opened in the scope 003 build; what it contains, how it is read and the permission check are built in scope 004
Key identity[].routing_profile: 'primary' is the default and only accepted value; 'replica' is refused with config.unsupported_value until scope 007

Name syntax and Path syntax of spec 0003: a name is 1 to 63 bytes of UTF-8 with no control character, compared byte for byte, never folded or trimmed; a path is 1 to 4096 bytes, starts with / and has no control character
Findings section of spec 0003 (six new codes in the family of the spec 0001 findings, all exit 1; config.missing_key keeps its meaning and is now also used inside entries)
Finding code config.invalid_value: a value has the right type but not the allowed syntax or range
Finding code config.duplicate_id: an id repeats an earlier id of the same table
Finding code config.unknown_reference: a key names a cluster or node that the file does not define, or expected_writer names a node of another cluster
Finding code config.duplicate_endpoint: a node has the host (compared without regard to ASCII case) and port of an earlier node
Finding code config.duplicate_identity: an identity has the principal and database of an earlier identity
Finding code config.unsupported_value: a value is known but not supported by this build (routing_profile = replica)

Location::KeyAt: the fourth finding location of spec 0003 (key plus line and column) for findings inside repeated tables; the human line is '<code> at <key>, line <line>, column <column>: <message>'; output_version stays 1

Validation order of spec 0003: steps 1 to 4 of spec 0001 stay; step 5 collects every finding in order (the three spec 0001 checks, the control keys, clusters, nodes, identities, then six cross checks whose skips keep one mistake from producing two findings)

Which code a bad value gets (spec 0003 table: a wrong shape or type is config.schema, a wrong syntax or range is config.invalid_value, routing_profile replica is config.unsupported_value, empty arrays are valid)

Public boundary added to pool-config by spec 0003: ValidatedConfig::control, clusters, nodes, identities and resolve_identity; ControlConfig, ClusterConfig, NodeConfig, IdentityRoute, SecretReference and RoutingProfile; hand written Debug prints identifiers only; no public constructor, Default or Deserialize
ValidatedConfig::resolve_identity(principal, database): the identity map lookup of spec 0003; an exact byte for byte pair, no wildcard and no default entry; it must not walk every entry

Fixtures of spec 0003 in crates/pool-config/tests/fixtures: valid-topology-minimal, valid-topology, valid-topology-names, ten invalid-topology-* files and secret-topology-values, built on a fifteen line base; positions were read from toml 1.2.1; the canary CANARY-9f2c7b1e is fake

The authority model in pool-control (spec 0003): a library with one dependency, pool-config; everything is a plain function over values; the caller reads the journal, the clock and the probes and passes what it found
classify_startup(config, probe) -> AuthorityState: classifies a start from what the journal reader found and from whether the configuration carries control.authority_id (the witness)
plan_bootstrap(config, probe, observations, now, expiry) -> Result<BootstrapPlan, BootstrapRefused>: decides whether the bootstrap command may write, for every configured cluster at once

writer_admission(config, state, cluster, observations, now, expiry) -> WriterAdmission: may a write go to a node of this cluster, and to which one; Open only when no reason applies, and then always the approved writer of the journal
StoreProbe enum (Absent, Unreadable, Present(StoredAuthority)): what the journal reader found; in the product only the journal reader that scope 004 places in pool-control builds one
StoredAuthority struct (authority_id, authority_revision, start_sequence, hold, clusters, quarantine) with public fields, because the journal reader has to fill it
Hold enum (None, RestorePending): the restore hold a journal carries when it came out of a supported backup
AuthorityState enum (Uninitialized, Unconfirmed, Missing, Unreadable, Mismatch, Held, Ready(Authority)); only Ready carries an Authority
Authority struct: private; only classify_startup makes one, so no state other than Ready can lead to an open admission
EligiblePrimary struct: the private result of an Open admission, with cluster(), node(), topology_epoch() and authority_revision()
Closed struct: private and never empty; reasons() gives each ClosedReason at most once, latches_conflict() says whether the daemon must set the conflict latch

BootstrapPlan struct: private; one ApprovedTopology per cluster with the expected_writer, the configured system identifier, the timeline the writer reported, epoch 1, every configured node as a member and no conflict latch

Fresh rule of spec 0003: per node the observation with the latest sampled_at counts (a tie is no evidence); it is fresh when sampled_at is not later than now and its age is less than the expiry; a stale or Failed observation is no evidence
Start classification table of spec 0003 (what the journal reader found, crossed with whether the configuration carries the authority witness)
AuthorityState Uninitialized: the journal is Absent and there is no witness; admission is Closed with authority.uninitialized
AuthorityState Unconfirmed: the journal is Present but the configuration carries no witness; Closed with authority.unconfirmed
AuthorityState Missing: the witness is set but the journal is Absent; Closed with authority.missing
AuthorityState Unreadable: the file cannot be opened, is not a POOL journal, has a newer schema, fails its integrity check or holds an inconsistent StoredAuthority; Closed with authority.unreadable
AuthorityState Mismatch: the journal is Present but the witness differs from its authority ID; Closed with authority.mismatch
AuthorityState Held: the witness equals the authority ID and the hold is restore_pending; Closed with authority.restore_pending
AuthorityState Ready: the witness equals the authority ID and the hold is none; the only state that carries an Authority and runs the ten writer admission checks
Writer admission reason 1, authority.cluster_unknown: the journal has no approved topology for this cluster, or the configuration has no such cluster; reported alone

Writer admission reason 2, authority.config_conflict: expected_writer is not the approved writer, or the configured system identifier is not the one in the journal, or a journal member is not a configured node of this cluster
Writer admission reason 3, authority.conflict_latched: the conflict latch of the cluster is set in the journal
Writer admission reason 4, authority.writer_quarantined: the approved writer is in the quarantine of its cluster
Writer admission reason 5, evidence.writer_missing: there is no fresh Reached observation of the approved writer; checks 6 to 8 are then skipped
Writer admission reason 6, evidence.writer_identity: the approved writer reports another system identifier than the journal
Writer admission reason 7, evidence.writer_in_recovery: the approved writer reports that it is in recovery
Writer admission reason 8, evidence.writer_timeline: the approved writer reports another timeline than the journal recorded
Writer admission reason 9, evidence.second_primary: another configured node, not quarantined, with a fresh observation and the system identifier of the journal reports that it is not in recovery
Writer admission reason 10, evidence.timeline_ahead: another configured node, not quarantined, with a fresh observation reports a timeline greater than the one the journal recorded for the writer

Three way agreement (spec 0003): the configuration, the journal and a fresh observation must name the same writer; the configuration cannot replace the journal (PRD-006 AC-3), the observation cannot replace either, and the journal alone is not enough without fresh evidence (0001 SC-8)

Positive conflict closes, silence about a replica does not (spec 0003): a second primary or a node on a later timeline closes writes; a replica that is down, slow or not yet probed does not, or one dead replica would stop every write
Quarantine is the reviewed answer (spec 0003): a quarantined node that reports itself as a primary does not close writes to the approved writer, and it never becomes eligible by itself

Conflict latch rule (spec 0003): Closed::latches_conflict() is true for evidence.second_primary or evidence.timeline_ahead; the daemon of scope 004 then sets the latch in the journal in one transaction; admission stays closed with authority.conflict_latched until an operation clears it (PRD-006 AC-2); an observation can add this restriction and never remove one
A member cannot be dropped by editing the file (spec 0003): a configuration that no longer lists a journal member is a conflict; removing a member is the detach operation of scope 009
The minimum durable writer check (spec 0003): scope 004 calls writer_admission when a session is admitted and again after the backend is acquired, before the lease is shown to the client

Bootstrap in spec 0003: the only way a journal comes into being; an explicit operator command, the daemon never creates a journal, so an empty directory authorizes nothing; stricter than admission because it needs every node once; the scope 004 command writes the journal in one transaction with a new random authority ID, revision 1, start sequence 0 and hold none, and prints the ID
Bootstrap refusal 1, bootstrap.store_present: the journal reader found anything but Absent
Bootstrap refusal 2, bootstrap.witness_present: the configuration carries control.authority_id; a journal existed once, so this is lost authority and not a first start
Bootstrap refusal 3, bootstrap.no_cluster: the configuration has no cluster
Bootstrap refusal 4, bootstrap.evidence_missing: some node of some cluster has no fresh Reached observation
Bootstrap refusal 5, bootstrap.identity_mismatch: some observed node reports another system identifier than its cluster configures
Bootstrap refusal 6, bootstrap.writer_in_recovery: the expected_writer of some cluster reports that it is in recovery
Bootstrap refusal 7, bootstrap.second_primary: a node other than the expected_writer reports that it is not in recovery
Bootstrap refusal 8, bootstrap.timeline_ahead: a node reports a timeline greater than that of the expected_writer of its cluster

The four walks of spec 0003: one test each in crates/pool-control/tests/walkthroughs.rs, sharing cluster main with the nodes pg1, pg2 and pg3, expected_writer pg1, an expiry of 6 seconds and a now of 100 seconds

Walk 1 clean startup (test walk_clean_startup): the first start is Uninitialized and closed; bootstrap plans main with writer pg1, timeline 1, epoch 1 or is refused (rows 2a to 2e); after bootstrap the state is Unconfirmed until the operator adds the witness, then Ready and Open

Walk 2 missing journal (test walk_missing_journal): a journal that is gone is Missing, a damaged one is Unreadable, another daemon's is Mismatch, and bootstrap is refused; the two ways out are restoring a backup or a deliberate new bootstrap, which forgets the quarantine and every membership decision

Walk 3 conflicting role evidence (test walk_conflicting_evidence): rows a to p from a Ready state; only full agreement opens; rows c, d and i latch a conflict; an unrecorded promotion never adopts pg2; rows j and k stay Open

Walk 4 restore of a backup taken before a promotion (test walk_restore_before_promotion): a supported backup carries the hold restore_pending and is Held; raw copies are caught by config conflict, missing writer, second primary or timeline ahead; the way out is the reconcile operation of scope 009, which gives the journal a new authority ID

The journal of spec 0003: journal.sqlite3 in control.state_directory (directory mode 0700, files 0600), one journal per daemon, WAL, synchronous FULL, foreign_keys ON, one writer, every mutation one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction; application_id 1347374924 (the bytes POOL) and user_version 1; built in scope 004
Journal schema version 1 of spec 0003: four STRICT tables, store, approved_topology, member and quarantine; the statements were run against SQLite 3.54.0 on 2026-11-15
Journal table store: one singleton row with authority_id (16 byte BLOB), authority_revision, start_sequence, hold (none or restore_pending) and created_unix_ms
Journal table approved_topology: per cluster_id the system_identifier (decimal text), approved_writer, writer_timeline, topology_epoch, conflict_latched, changed_revision and changed_unix_ms
Journal table member: rows of (cluster_id, node_id) with changed_revision; it holds the nodes of each cluster, the approved writer among them
Journal table quarantine: rows of (cluster_id, node_id) with since_epoch, changed_revision and changed_unix_ms

Journal migrations of spec 0003: forward only, numbered, one transaction each; a file with a version above what the binary knows is Unreadable; a failed migration leaves the version and the daemon closed; later slices add tables by migration

Journal start rule of spec 0003: the daemon first reads the journal without writing and classifies the start; only in Ready does it apply migrations and advance start_sequence by one; in every other state it writes nothing to the file

How the journal reader maps what it finds (spec 0003): no file is Absent; an unopenable file, a wrong application ID, a newer version, a failed quick_check, a missing store row, a writer without a member row or a value out of range is Unreadable; anything else is Present

Operation records rules fixed by spec 0003 (SEC-7, R-18): the operation row is durable before the first effect outside the journal; every phase change is one transaction; rows in a non final phase are reconciled at start without repeating an effect; the same caller, kind and request ID give the same row (PRD-010 AC-1); writer change, new epoch, quarantine and outcome are one transaction (PRD-007 AC-4)

Value sourcing table of spec 0003 (finding fields from pool-config constants and toml spans; system_identifier and expected_writer written by the operator; the authority ID from 16 random bytes; observed role, identity and timeline from the probe of 004; now from the monotonic clock; StoreProbe from the journal reader)

Security model of spec 0003: the configuration file belongs to the operator, the state directory and journal to the service account alone; a backend login is chosen only by the identity map from a verified principal; the configuration holds references, never secrets; a lost, foreign or restored journal is detected and keeps admission closed

Workspace and guards section of spec 0003: crates/pool-control becomes the third workspace member (inherits the five workspace fields, depends on pool-config with workspace = true, workspace lints, no dev-dependencies and no build script); apps/pool does not depend on pool-control yet

Baseline file changes of spec 0003 in tools/repo-check/baseline: add pool-control to lock-packages.txt (W1), remove crates/pool-control from forbidden-paths.txt (W2), add 'pool-control -> pool-config' to internal-dependencies.txt (W5); forbidden-source-patterns.txt does not change

W4 addition of spec 0003 (the answer to spec 0002 Follow-up 10): every [[package]] entry of the root Cargo.lock without a source line must be a member written in members; the test helper gives non members a registry source line; reading the dependency edges from the lockfile is the runner up

prove-checks.sh case 17 in spec 0003: it replaces 'planned' in the first line of the scope 003 file, which no longer holds the word once feature 3 is in-progress; point the case at docs/scope/004-one-real-primary-path.md

0001 AC-1 (two members), 0001 AC-12 (two workspace packages in the lockfile) and 0001 AC-13 (crates/pool-control does not exist) describe the first build and their evidence stands; from this slice on 0003 AC-13 is the current statement

Tests and who owns them (spec 0003): the cargo test harness only; pool-config validate.rs and unit tests, apps/pool check_config.rs, pool-control walkthroughs.rs and admission_model.rs, compile_fail documentation tests, and the W4 cases in pool-repo-check

The small domain of 0003 AC-12 (test open_only_on_full_agreement in admission_model.rs): 8192 combinations of expected_writer, approved writer, pg3 quarantine, conflict latch and eight observations per node, compared with an expected answer computed by a rule written separately from the code under test

compile_fail documentation tests of spec 0003: comparing a NodeId with a ClusterId or a TopologyEpoch with an AuthorityRevision (AC-6); a struct literal of Authority, EligiblePrimary, Closed or BootstrapPlan written outside the crate (AC-12)

Document corrections of spec 0003 (seven items in files the spec does not own: the engineering standards shared conventions row and workspace paragraph, repository structure, the glossary rows Observation and Approved writer, docs/index.md, agent and contributor files, and the pointer notes in spec 0001 and 0002)

Build plan of spec 0003 (a tracer bullet: a workspace that still passes every check with the new member, then the configuration path from file to finding, then the authority rules, then the evidence; each step ends with a commit named 'spec 0003 step <n>')

0003 Build plan step 1: Workspace member and guards (crates/pool-control manifest and lib.rs, root Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, three baseline files, the W4 lockfile check with two tests, case 17 pointed at the scope 004 file, Status set to In Progress); satisfies AC-13
0003 Build plan step 2: Identifier and generation types in crates/pool-config/src with unit tests and the two compile_fail documentation tests; satisfies AC-6

0003 Build plan step 3: Configuration keys in pool-config (keys, findings, validation order, public boundary with resolve_identity and hand written Debug, every fixture, validate.rs, the Location::KeyAt arm in apps/pool/src/report.rs); satisfies AC-5 and the library half of AC-1 to AC-4
0003 Build plan step 4: The new finding line in apps/pool (Location::KeyAt rendering in the human and JSON formats, check_config.rs with every new fixture in both formats); completes AC-1 to AC-4

0003 Build plan step 5: Authority model in pool-control (the types, classify_startup, plan_bootstrap, writer_admission, walkthroughs.rs, admission_model.rs, a restart rule comment on every public record type); needs steps 1, 2 and 3; satisfies AC-7 to AC-12 and the code half of AC-14
0003 Build plan step 6: Document corrections (items 1 to 4), evidence scripts/check.sh docs; completes AC-14

0003 Build plan step 7: Evidence (check.sh all, prove-checks.sh, check.sh fuzz and the cargo metadata command) recorded with commands, results and revision in docs/specs/0003-control-and-session-data-model/verify.md; evidence for AC-1 to AC-14
Parallel sessions of the spec 0003 Build plan: step 1 and steps 2 to 4 share no file and can run at the same time; step 5 needs both; steps 6 and 7 come last

Positive consequences of spec 0003: the rule against R-19 exists as tested code before any socket does; every state short of full agreement leads to closed; a missing, a foreign and a restored journal are three named states; findings name key and place; default telemetry has its allowed names; no third party package is added (still sixteen)

Tradeoff of spec 0003: after a bootstrap, and again after a reconcile, the operator must copy the authority ID into the configuration before POOL admits anything; that step tells a first start from a lost journal
Tradeoff of spec 0003: after a promotion (010) the configuration must name the new writer before writes open again; until then admission is closed with authority.config_conflict

Tradeoff of spec 0003: a raw file copy of the journal carries no hold; with the old writer up and unfenced and no node on the newer timeline reachable, POOL cannot tell and opens writes to the old writer; fencing and the supported backup are the protection; a rollback of the whole proxy VM is the same case
Tradeoff of spec 0003: a stale configuration without the witness together with a lost journal looks like a first start; bootstrap then still needs fitting evidence from every node
Tradeoff of spec 0003: a new bootstrap after a lost journal forgets the quarantine and every membership decision
Tradeoff of spec 0003: until scope 009 exists nothing clears a conflict latch and nothing removes a member, so such a cluster stays closed until the member is put back or the operator bootstraps anew
Tradeoff of spec 0003: the configuration is trusted; pointing the host of a node at another machine makes POOL probe that machine; the journal records node IDs, not addresses
Tradeoff of spec 0003: bootstrap needs every configured node reachable once; a node that is down has to be repaired or taken out of the configuration first
Tradeoff of spec 0003: pool-control is built before anything calls it, so its interface may need to change when scope 004 connects real inputs; the rules should not
Tradeoff of spec 0003: findings inside entries name the key and the place but still not the text
Tradeoff of spec 0003: the identity map is exact, so ten databases for one principal are ten entries
Tradeoff of spec 0003: the journal schema is fixed here and first run by scope 004; a flaw found then is a change to this spec

Neutral consequences of spec 0003: key names, finding codes, the fourth finding line, reason names, the journal file name, its marks and its schema are contracts from now on; node means a configured PostgreSQL server everywhere; the first secret reference key arrives here and its reading in 004
0003 Follow-up 1: spec 0001 needs three notes that point here, applied by the lead (credential_file as the first secret reference key, the fourth finding line, the identifier and generation types)

0003 Follow-up 2: spec 0002 needs three notes that point here, applied by the lead (its Follow-up 10 is answered by Workspace and guards, the baseline block shows the first build, case 17 now names the scope 004 file)

0003 Follow-up 3: scope 004 adopts SQLite, the first native code in the product: boundary review, a person's decision on any new license, the NOTICE file, and how one writer runs without breaking the thread rule of W3

0003 Follow-up 4: scope 004 fixes the bootstrap command, the probe and its queries, the probe period and observation expiry keys, the file permission checks and how each authentication method names the verified principal; it must report the current timeline, lock the state directory exclusively and offer a way to read the authority ID again
0003 Follow-up 5: scope 005 names the trigger that advances a credential generation before a reload route exists, as the dependency plan asks

0003 Follow-up 6: scope 009 builds the backup that sets the hold, the reconcile operation, the operation and audit tables and the way a cluster is added to an existing journal; until then there is no supported backup and the only way out of a lost journal is a new bootstrap

0003 Follow-up 7: scope 010 makes 'the configuration names the new writer' a step of the promotion procedure and decides whether the promotion plan binds the authority revision as well as the topology epoch
0003 Follow-up 8: the risk register rows R-18 and R-19 can name the tests of this spec as their first evidence once the build is verified; that edit belongs to the Document it box
0003 Follow-up 9: scope 012 needs ordered epochs across several proxies; the authority ID plus the topology epoch is the local form of that; a journal per daemon is not merged into a shared authority
